purpose: Select disruption, protection or recovery action sets under explicit budgets instead of ranking components independently.

mathematical_formulation.protection: min_{p in P(B)} max_{y in Y(B)} L(G,p,y)

unlock_rule: Disabled until action costs, budgets and a supported performance evaluator are provided. Worst-case decisions are not natural-hazard probabilities.

primary_sources.citation: Wood (1993), Deterministic network interdiction, Mathematical and Computer Modelling.
Israeli and Wood (2002), Shortest-path network interdiction, Networks.
Scaparra and Church (2008), A bilevel mixed-integer program for critical infrastructure protection planning. Computers & Operations Research, 35(6), 1905-1923.

known_limitations: Set-based optimisation can be computationally hard.
Solver status, bound and optimality gap are mandatory.
An adversarial worst case is not a forecast.
